title: Sunny and the Creek Lullaby
description: Little Sonny the quokka follows the sound of the creek and finds the most peaceful lullaby in the bush. A gentle, flowing bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One evening, just as the sky was beginning to turn pink, Sunny heard a sound that made him stop walking.

A soft, steady, gurgling sound.

He turned toward it and followed it through the low scrub, stepping carefully between the rocks, until he came to the creek.

It wasn't a big creek. Just a small, quiet one, winding between mossy rocks and trailing ferns. But the sound it made as it moved over the stones was one of the most beautiful things Sunny had ever heard.

Gurgle. Trickle. Rush. Pause. Gurgle.

It never stopped. It never needed to think about it. It just kept going, perfectly and naturally, without any effort at all.

Sunny sat down on a smooth, flat rock at the water's edge and listened.

The water was very clear. He could see the rounded pebbles at the bottom, and tiny water beetles moving among them. A dragonfly hovered, perfectly still, then zipped away.

The pink sky reflected in the slow pools between the stones.

Sunny took off his shoes — well, he didn't have shoes, but if he had, he would have — and dipped his toes in.

The water was cold and clear and real.

He sat there as the sky turned from pink to purple to the first soft dark of evening, listening to the creek's endless lullaby.

It sang: here, and now, and all is well, and keep going, and rest.

Sunny listened. He heard all of it.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, small and singing creek. Goodnight, flowing, peaceful night.
